sections.content: How many people are "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists"?

17,325 people

were counted on the census as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists give advice on careers or occupations, training courses and related matters, direct school leavers and other job seekers into employment and assess their progress.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists", 13.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" included:

  • other drivers and transport operatives
  • credit controllers
  • fork-lift truck drivers

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" there were more women than men (75.8% compared with 24.2%).

This means "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 24.2% and women made up 75.8% of "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" included:

  • podiatrists
  • credit controllers
  • finance officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists", 13.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (68.3% compared with 31.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.2%) than self-employed (7.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
